source_text: Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Ποῦ συνέρχεσθε, Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἔνθα ἑκάστῳ προαίρεσις καὶ δύναμίς ἐστι. Πάντως γὰρ νομίζεις ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ συνέρχεσθαι ἡμᾶς πάντας; Οὐχ οὕτως δέ· διότι ὁ Θεὸς τῶν Χριστιανῶν τόπῳ οὐ περιγράφεται, ἀλλὰ, ἀόρατος ὢν, τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν πληροῖ, καὶ πανταχοῦ ὑπὸ τῶν πιστῶν προσκυνεῖται καὶ δοξάζεται. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Εἰπὲ ποῦ συνέρχεσθε, ἢ εἰς ποῖον τόπον ἀθροίζεις τοὺς μαθητάς σου; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἐγὼ ἐπάνω μένω τινὸς Μαρτίνου τοῦ Τιμιοτίνου βαλανείου, καὶ παρὰ πάντα τὸν χρόνον τοῦτον· (ἐπεδήμησα δὲ τῇ Ῥωμαίων πόλει τοῦτο δεύτερον) καὶ οὐ γινώσκω ἄλλην τινὰ συνέλευσιν εἰ μὴ τὴν ἐκείνου. Καὶ εἴ τις ἐβούλετο ἀφικνεῖσθαι παρ' ἐμοὶ, ἐκοινώνουν αὐτῷ τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας λόγων. Ῥουστικὸς εἶπεν· Οὐκοῦν λοιπὸν Χριστιανὸς εἶ; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ναὶ, Χριστιανός εἰμι.
thought_title: Where Christians gather and Justin's confession
orientation: Rusticus the prefect continues interrogating Justin, pressing him on where Christians assemble, and Justin answers that God is not confined to a place, then admits he stays above a certain bath and finally confesses plainly that he is a Christian.
pass_a_gloss: Rusticus the prefect said: Where do you gather? Justin said: Where to each one there is choice and ability. For do you think that we all gather to the same place? Not so, but because the God of the Christians is not circumscribed by a place, but, being invisible, fills heaven and earth, and everywhere by the faithful he is worshipped and glorified. Rusticus the prefect said: Say where you gather, or into what place you assemble your disciples. Justin said: I myself stay above a certain bath of Martinus son of Timiotinus, and during all this time (and I have sojourned in the city of the Romans this second time), and I know no other meeting except that of him. And if anyone wished to come to me, I shared with him the words of the truth. Rusticus said: So then, are you a Christian? Justin said: Yes, I am a Christian.

choices.term: Ἔνθα ἑκάστῳ προαίρεσις καὶ δύναμίς ἐστι
choices.english: Where to each one there is choice and ability
choices.why: Keeps the abstract nouns προαίρεσις and δύναμις as subjects with the dative of possession, preserving the literal structure and the sense that the place is wherever each person has the will and power to meet.
rejected: Wherever each one has the will and the power
Where each one chooses and is able

choices.english: is not circumscribed by a place
choices.why: περιγράφεται is a technical term for being bounded or enclosed; 'circumscribed' preserves the spatial metaphor and the passive voice.
rejected: is not confined to a place
is not limited by a place

choices.term: ἐπάνω μένω τινὸς Μαρτίνου τοῦ Τιμιοτίνου βαλανείου
choices.english: I myself stay above a certain bath of Martinus son of Timiotinus
choices.why: ἐπάνω with the genitive means 'above' or 'over'; μένω means 'I stay' or 'I dwell'; the genitive chain identifies the bath's owner and his father, kept literal.
rejected: I live above the bath of a certain Martinus, son of Timiotinus
I am staying over the bath of Martinus Timiotinus

choices.term: ἐκοινώνουν αὐτῷ τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας λόγων
choices.english: I shared with him the words of the truth
choices.why: κοινωνέω with the genitive means to share in or impart something; 'words of the truth' keeps the article-noun-genitive structure and the sense of Christian teaching.
rejected: I communicated to him the words of truth
I imparted to him the words of the truth

choices.why: Ναί is a strong affirmative; the word order with the predicate first is preserved, and 'Christian' follows the glossary.

pass_b_english: The prefect Rusticus said, "Where do you gather?" Justin said, "Where each one chooses and is able. Do you really think we all gather in the same place? Not so, because the God of the Christians is not circumscribed by a place, but, being invisible, fills heaven and earth, and everywhere is worshipped and glorified by the faithful." The prefect Rusticus said, "Tell me where you gather, or in what place you assemble your disciples." Justin said, "I myself stay above a certain bath of Martinus son of Timiotinus, and have done so for all this time—this is my second sojourn in the city of the Romans—and I know no other meeting place than his. And if anyone wished to come to me, I shared with him the words of the truth." Rusticus said, "So then, you are a Christian?" Justin said, "Yes, I am a Christian."

problems.quote: Where each person has the choice and the ability
problems.why: Justin answers 'where do you gather?' with individual choice, but 'ability' is nonsensical as place.
problems.fix: 'Where each one chooses and is able' (i.e., wherever they can).

problems.quote: the true teachings, those of the Christians
problems.why: Singular and plural alternate for the same concept; reader may distinguish them.

edits.old: Where each person has the choice and the ability.
edits.new: Where each one chooses and is able.

fixed: The English 'Where each person has the choice and the ability' is awkward and 'ability' as a place is nonsensical. The source 'Ἔνθα ἑκάστῳ προαίρεσις καὶ δύναμίς ἐστι' means 'where each one has choice and ability', i.e., wherever each one chooses and is able. The suggested fix 'Where each one chooses and is able' is accurate and natural.

The reported glossary problem about 'the true teachings, those of the Christians' does not appear in the provided English text. The English uses 'the words of the truth' (τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας λόγων), which is singular 'truth' and consistent. No edit needed.
